region: Gualtallary, Tupungato · Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina
about: The Zuccardi story begins in 1963, when engineer Alberto “Tito” Zuccardi planted a vineyard in Mendoza to demonstrate an irrigation system he had invented. His son José Alberto took over in 1985, and grandson Sebastián led the family into the high Uco Valley, planting the first estate vineyard there in 2007 and founding a soil research department. Their stone-and-concrete winery in Paraje Altamira opened in 2016 and was named World’s Best Vineyard three years running, from 2019 to 2021.

Polígonos is Zuccardi’s series of village wines. Each one portrays a single district of the Uco Valley, and the name comes from the irregular shapes the vineyard plots make on a map. Gualtallary sits high in Tupungato, around 1,360 metres, at the foot of the Andes’ Cordón del Plata. Its soils are layered sand, caliche and stones, rich in calcium carbonate. The grapes move by gravity and ferment with native yeasts in concrete. The wine then ages in concrete and barrels and is bottled unfiltered.

2020 was a fast, demanding harvest, with yields 10–20% below average. Importer notes describe pure dark fruit, plum and blackcurrant, with earthy herbs and spice and a long, fragrant finish; the winery highlights its herbal character, fresh red fruit, lively acidity and fine tannins. Zuccardi makes these wines to show the place rather than the cellar: picking each plot and soil type separately, and using concrete to keep the focus on Gualtallary’s mountain fruit.
